purpose: mechanical normalization of Annotator A's natural-language calibration labels into the frozen world-fact verdict vocabulary; the original record annotator-a-calibration-01.md is not modified
mapper: adjudication phase (executed by opencode agent under experiment owner direction)
mapping_rules: Annotator A names a concrete repository-local target (repository path or repository qualified symbol) with no stated indeterminacy -> ONE_VALID_TARGET

Annotator A affirms the relation but the stated referent is external to the repository (system library / C++ standard library / Python builtin or stdlib module) or is a non-symbol binding (preprocessing macro without repository target, Python local variable / parameter / attribute), with no valid repository candidate -> NO_VALID_TARGET

Annotator A affirms the relation but explicitly states the in-repository definition cannot be determined from the blinded package -> INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE (target-level; relation existence is affirmed)

policy.note: All 25 labels mapped uniquely from the per-case table. The table is authoritative; Annotator A's prose observation 2 (12 repo-local targets, 6 imports + 6 calls) is inconsistent with A's own table (11: 7 imports + 4 calls) and was not used for mapping.

record_level_observations: Annotator A intentionally assigned no formal relation_verdict (source record line 9): the two permitted vocabularies depend on the hidden system status. This normalization therefore emits blind world-fact verdicts only; the join to stratum-specific enums happens later.
Prose-vs-table count inconsistency in Annotator A's observation 2 documented above.
